about: Intercept master list (a Declass daily puzzle). Each group: id (never reused), link (the typed line shown when it locks), difficulty (easy, medium, hard; never shown to players), cards (every posted card the group can be dealt from), alsoFits (posted cards that also fit the link but are never dealt in it, so the conflict check keeps them off any board that holds this group), source (what backs the link), added, and optional vetoed. Only cards that have already posted are ever listed (a Name This card once its answer is public). Maintained by the Tuesday analytics review (Analytics doc, Intercept master list).

groups.link: All three photos show a warship.
groups.source: Photo credits in each record: Kearny (twice), Tirpitz, HMS Seraph (Cherchell), Musashi, Johnston, Hornet under attack, HMS Petard (U-559), Reuben James. Samar shows ships through smoke and Leyte a landing craft, so both are kept off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: the cruiser Nachi under attack (Manila Bay). The Fireball deck, the Torch landing craft, and the captured Odenwald are kept off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three photos show aircraft.
groups.source: Photo credits: TDR-1 in flight, B-17D at Wright Field, NA-73X prototype, B-25s over the Western Desert, Mosquito FB.VIs. Hornet's photo shows a diving Japanese bomber and Gable's a B-17 waist gun. Added 10 Nov 2026: the Mosquito Name This card (FB.VIs setting out from Thorney Island) and FR-1 Fireballs on the deck of USS Ranger.

groups.link: All three photos show a national leader.
groups.source: Photo credits: Tojo (prime minister from 18 Oct 1941), Metaxas (prime minister of Greece), Churchill (prime minister), Roosevelt (president). Roosevelt appears in both draft photos (Stimson drawing the first capsule with Roosevelt at the microphones; Roosevelt signing the act), so both are in the group. Philippine President Osmena waded ashore with MacArthur at Leyte. Added 10 Nov 2026: Churchill (End of the Beginning) and Roosevelt on both election cards. Eisenhower, a general who later became president, stays off boards with this group. The draft lottery story and its spec sheet are one event, so only the story is dealt.

groups.link: All three are from the war in the Pacific.
groups.source: Places in each record: Leyte, Bougainville, off Samar, Santa Cruz Islands, Sibuyan Sea, Central Pacific. Tojo led Japan into the Pacific war, and This Is the Army toured the Pacific, so both stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: Manila Bay. Sorge was hanged in Tokyo and the Fireball landing came after the war, so both stay off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three are from the war in North Africa.
groups.source: Places in each record: Cherchell, Algeria (the run up to Operation Torch) and El Alamein, Egypt. U-559 was sunk off Port Said, Egypt, so it stays off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: Rommel retreats from Alamein and the Torch landings in Morocco and Algeria. Churchill's End of the Beginning speech hailed Alamein, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three are from the Second Battle of El Alamein.
groups.source: The battle ran 23 Oct to 11 Nov 1942. Records: the opening barrage (23 Oct), the Sherman's first action (24 Oct), Outpost Snipe (27 Oct), Rommel's counterattack (28 Oct). Medium, not hard, because every card prints El Alamein as its place. Added 10 Nov 2026: Rommel retreats from Alamein (4 Nov). Churchill's speech hailing the victory stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three took place in the North Atlantic.
groups.source: Kearny was torpedoed off Iceland (17 Oct 1941); Reuben James was sunk near Iceland escorting HX 156 (31 Oct 1941). Tirpitz in Norway and FDR's speech about Kearny stay off boards with this group. Odenwald was taken near the equator, so it stays off boards with this group (10 Nov 2026).

groups.link: All three took place in the Philippines.
groups.source: Red Beach, Leyte; off Samar (Samar and Johnston); the Sibuyan Sea, where Musashi was sunk. Added 10 Nov 2026: the carrier strike on Manila Bay.

groups.link: All three photos show a destroyer.
groups.source: Photo credits: USS Kearny (Gleaves class, twice), USS Johnston (Fletcher class), USS Reuben James (Clemson class), HMS Petard (P class) on the U-559 card. Samar shows destroyer escorts making smoke. Medium because it takes knowing ship types.

groups.link: All three involve American bombers.
groups.source: B-17 (Rickenbacker's ditching), Gable (flew in B-17s, photo beside a B-17 waist gun), the Alamein counterattack card (B-25s). Hornet launched the Doolittle B-25s and the TDR-1 carried a bomb under an Avenger's control, so both stay off boards with this group. U.S. Navy bombers sank Nachi in Manila Bay, so that card stays off boards with this group (10 Nov 2026).

groups.link: All three involve Franklin D. Roosevelt.
groups.source: Navy Day address (27 Oct 1941); Roosevelt watched the draft lottery and signed the Selective Training and Service Act (records 025 and 026). He approved the WAVES change, named the United Nations, and spoke about Kearny and Reuben James, so those stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: his third and fourth term wins. He signed the order that led to camps such as Tule Lake, so it stays off boards with this group. The draft lottery story and its spec sheet are one event, so only the story is dealt.

groups.link: All three are remembered for a famous line.
groups.source: MacArthur's "I have returned" (Leyte), Churchill's "For the morning will come" (broadcast to France), Roosevelt's "The shooting has started", Metaxas's "Then it is war" (Ochi). The UN Charter's "We the peoples" and Evans's "fighting ship" stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: Churchill's "the end of the beginning". Hitler's "a few small pockets left" stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three involve German U-boats.
groups.source: U-568 torpedoed Kearny (17 Oct 1941), U-552 sank Reuben James (31 Oct 1941), HMS Petard forced U-559 to the surface (30 Oct 1942). FDR's Navy Day speech was about Kearny, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three involve a submarine.
groups.source: Mark Clark landed at Cherchell from the submarine HMS Seraph (22 Oct 1942); U-559; U-568 hit Kearny; U-552 sank Reuben James.

groups.link: All three are from the Battle of Leyte Gulf.
groups.source: The Battle off Samar (25 Oct 1944, Taffy 3 and Johnston) and the Battle of the Sibuyan Sea (24 Oct 1944, where Musashi was sunk) are two of the four main actions of Leyte Gulf. The Leyte landing set the battle off, so it stays off boards with this group. Nachi, sunk in Manila Bay, had fought at Surigao Strait, so that card stays off boards with this group (10 Nov 2026).

groups.link: Each ship was named for a man of the U.S. Navy.
groups.source: Navy ship histories (DANFS): Kearny for Commodore Lawrence Kearny, Reuben James for the boatswain's mate of the Barbary Wars, Johnston for John V. Johnston, Union Navy officer. Tirpitz was named for a German admiral and makes a fair red herring.

groups.link: All three involve the United States backing Britain before Pearl Harbor.
groups.source: Kearny went to help a British convoy's escorts (SC 48); Reuben James was escorting HX 156 toward Britain; North American built the Mustang to a British order in 1940. FDR's speech about Kearny stays off boards with this group. Vetoed by Brian on the Scoreboard, 28 Oct 2026; kept so it is never added again.

groups.link: In all three, the Allies captured something German.
groups.source: Aachen's garrison surrendered and was marched off (21 Oct 1944); Petard's boarders took U-559's codebooks (30 Oct 1942); the White Sands photo came from a captured V-2 (24 Oct 1946). The Nuremberg defendants were in Allied custody, and the Sherman record quotes a captured German document, so both stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: General von Thoma, captured at El Alamein (photo with Montgomery). USS Omaha seized the German Odenwald before the U.S. was at war, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three involve the Royal Air Force.
groups.source: Mosquitoes struck the Aarhus Gestapo headquarters (31 Oct 1944); the RAF flew the first Mustangs; an RAF reconnaissance plane photographed Tirpitz on 18 Oct 1944 and RAF Lancasters sank her that November. The Desert Air Force bombed Rommel's panzers and flew over the Alamein barrage, so those cards stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: the Mosquito Name This card. The RAF bombed ahead of Supercharge and over the Alamein breakthrough, so those two also stay off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three involve the Royal Navy.
groups.source: HMS Petard sank U-559; HMS Seraph carried Mark Clark to Cherchell; the Royal Navy hunted Tirpitz for years (X-craft and Fleet Air Arm attacks, 1943 and 1944). Added 10 Nov 2026: Torch. The Royal Navy carried and covered the Oran and Algiers landings.

groups.link: Each involves a commander who won his nation's highest award for valor.
groups.source: Lt. Col. Victor Turner won the Victoria Cross for Outpost Snipe (London Gazette, 20 Nov 1942). Cmdr. Ernest E. Evans of USS Johnston won the Medal of Honor, posthumously, for the Battle off Samar (NHHC). MacArthur already held the Medal of Honor (1942) and the 1943 X-craft attack on Tirpitz won two VCs, so those cards stay off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each is a story of Americans and the British working together.
groups.source: Mark Clark, an American general, landed from the British submarine HMS Seraph (dispatch No. 011). The Shermans at Alamein were American built tanks rushed to Britain's Eighth Army after Tobruk fell (No. 014). North American Aviation designed the Mustang for a British order (No. 020). Kearny's convoy work, the Nuremberg prosecution, and the UN also fit loosely, so they stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: Torch, the joint American and British landings. Eisenhower, Supreme Allied Commander, stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves men later tried for war crimes.
groups.source: The Nuremberg indictment named 24 leading Nazis (No. 003). Hideki Tojo was tried by the International Military Tribunal for the Far East and executed in December 1948 (IMTFE judgment). Dormant until a third posted card fits.

groups.link: Each is tied to the city of Tokyo.
groups.source: Tojo became prime minister in Tokyo (No. 004). USS Hornet launched the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo in April 1942 (No. 019, 'Doolittle's carrier lost'). Dormant until a third posted card fits. Added 10 Nov 2026: Richard Sorge, hanged at Sugamo Prison in Tokyo (No. 044). Now live.

groups.link: In each, aircraft attacked warships.
groups.source: Japanese carrier planes struck USS Hornet at Santa Cruz (No. 019). RAF Lancasters attacked Tirpitz in September, October, and November 1944, the last raid sinking her. Taffy 3's aircraft attacked Kurita's ships off Samar while kamikazes struck the escort carriers (No. 017). Johnston also fits loosely. Added 10 Nov 2026: U.S. carrier planes sank the cruiser Nachi in Manila Bay (No. 039).

groups.link: All three involve Winston Churchill.
groups.source: Churchill's broadcast to France (No. 010). Churchill called Tirpitz The Beast (the Name This clue). Churchill was with Roosevelt at the White House when Tobruk fell in June 1942, and the Shermans at Alamein were the United States' answer to his plea (No. 014). Alamein and Torch also involve him, so they stay off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: the End of the Beginning speech. Rommel's retreat and Torch stay off boards with this group.

groups.link: All three involve France.
groups.source: Churchill's broadcast to the French people (No. 010). Mark Clark met French General Charles Mast in French Algeria (No. 011). France was one of the four prosecuting powers at the International Military Tribunal (No. 003). The UN (France a permanent member) also fits loosely. Added 10 Nov 2026: Torch landed in French North Africa against Vichy forces, and Patton's Lorraine offensive was fought in France.

groups.link: All three took place in the continental United States.
groups.source: The tin can order and the WAVES decision were national U.S. orders (Nos. 005 and 006); the V-2 flew from White Sands, New Mexico (No. 016); the Mustang first flew at Mines Field, Los Angeles (No. 020); FDR spoke in Washington (No. 022). This Is the Army closed in Hawaii, then a territory, so it stays off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: the X-10 reactor (Oak Ridge, Tennessee), Tule Lake (California), and both Roosevelt election cards (Hyde Park, New York, and Washington). The draft lottery story and its spec sheet are one event, so only the story is dealt.

groups.link: Each honors service by Americans from a minority group.
groups.source: The WAVES opened to Black women in October 1944 (No. 006); the 442nd Regimental Combat Team, Japanese American Nisei, rescued the Lost Battalion (No. 027); Navajo code talkers served with the 3rd Marine Division on Bougainville (No. 032). This Is the Army had an integrated cast, so it stays off boards with this group. Tule Lake held Japanese Americans, so it stays off boards with this group (10 Nov 2026).

groups.link: Each is tied to Hollywood.
groups.source: Clark Gable was Hollywood's leading man before joining the Army Air Forces (Name This, 28 Oct). This Is the Army became a 1943 Warner Bros. film with Ronald Reagan (No. 012). Howard Hughes produced and directed Hollywood films such as Hell's Angels (1930) before the H-4 flew (No. 034). Vetoed by Brian on the Scoreboard, 4 Nov 2026; kept so it is never added again.

groups.link: Each involves a Medal of Honor earned in that very action.
groups.source: Cmdr. Ernest E. Evans of USS Johnston, off Samar, 25 Oct 1944 (NHHC). Sgt. Robert A. Owens, 3rd Marine Division, Cape Torokina, 1 Nov 1943, posthumous. Pvt. George Sakato and Pvt. Barney Hajiro of the 442nd, near Biffontaine on 29 Oct 1944 during the drive to the Lost Battalion (awarded 2000; Army citations). MacArthur (Leyte), Doolittle (Hornet's raid), and Rickenbacker (the B-17 ditching) held the medal for other actions, so those stay off boards with this group. Medals of Honor were earned in the Torch landings at Port Lyautey, so that card stays off boards with this group (10 Nov 2026).

groups.link: Each involves a wartime secret the Allies guarded.
groups.source: The U-559 codebooks let Bletchley Park break the U-boat cipher, kept secret as part of Ultra for decades (No. 028). The Navajo code stayed secret until 1968 (No. 032). Mark Clark's meeting at Cherchell was a secret mission before Operation Torch (No. 011). The U.S. Office of Censorship kept balloon bomb landings out of the press until May 1945 (No. 035). The Fu-Go Spec Sheet is the same subject, so it stays off boards with this group. Added 10 Nov 2026: the X-10 reactor, part of the secret Manhattan Project. Torch was a guarded secret too, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves one of the largest machines of its kind ever built.
groups.source: Musashi and her sister Yamato were the largest battleships ever built (Name This, 24 Oct). The H-4 Hercules had the widest wingspan of any aircraft to fly until 2019 (No. 034). Tirpitz and Bismarck were the largest battleships built by a European navy (Name This, 18 Oct). Taffy 3 faced Yamato off Samar (No. 017); Johnston fought the same fleet, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves an ultimatum that was refused.
groups.source: Metaxas refused Mussolini's ultimatum on 28 Oct 1940 (No. 023). The U.S. 1st Infantry Division sent Aachen's garrison a surrender ultimatum on 10 Oct 1944, and it was refused; the city held until 21 Oct (No. 009; U.S. Army official history, Siegfried Line Campaign). Dormant until a third posted card fits.

groups.link: All three took place on or near Bougainville.
groups.source: Places in each record: the TDR-1 drone strike near Bougainville (No. 008), the Cape Torokina landing on Empress Augusta Bay (No. 031), and the Navajo code talkers on Bougainville (No. 032). Medium, not hard, because every card prints Bougainville.

groups.link: All three photos show an aircraft carrier.
groups.source: Photo credits: USS Hornet under attack at Santa Cruz, the escort carrier USS Gambier Bay making smoke off Samar, FR-1 Fireballs on the deck of USS Ranger. Approved by Brian, 7 Nov 2026.

groups.link: All three photos show troops landing from the sea.
groups.source: Photo credits: MacArthur wading ashore at Leyte, the first wave heading for the beach at Empress Augusta Bay, a landing craft heading for the beaches at Oran. Approved by Brian, 7 Nov 2026.

groups.link: Each involves Admiral William F. Halsey.
groups.source: Halsey led the Hornet task force on the Doolittle Raid and, as South Pacific commander, ordered the carriers into the Santa Cruz battle; his Third Fleet planes sank Musashi, his run north left Taffy 3 alone off Samar, and his Third Fleet carriers (McCain's Task Force 38) struck Manila Bay. His fleet covered Leyte and he ordered the Bougainville landing, so those stay off boards with this group; Halsey Hits Manila (13 Nov) prints his name and belongs in alsoFits. Johnston is the same battle as the Samar card, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each took to the air built mostly of wood or paper.
groups.source: The Mosquito was built mostly of wood (its clue); the H-4 Hercules was built mostly of laminated birch because of wartime limits on metal (No. 034); Fu-Go balloons were made of mulberry paper glued with konnyaku paste (No. 035). The TDR-1 had a steel tube frame under molded wood, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves the U.S. Navy confronting Germany before Pearl Harbor.
groups.source: U-568 torpedoed USS Kearny (17 Oct 1941), U-552 sank USS Reuben James (31 Oct 1941), and USS Omaha and USS Somers seized the German blockade runner Odenwald (6 Nov 1941), all before the U.S. entered the war. FDR's Navy Day speech about Kearny stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves a man who would later become president of the United States.
groups.source: Harry S. Truman rides beside Roosevelt after the 1944 election (No. 043; president April 1945). Eisenhower, president from 1953, visits the front (No. 049) and was the Allied commander in chief for Torch (No. 045). Mark Clark was Eisenhower's deputy for Torch and Ronald Reagan starred in the film of This Is the Army, so both stay off boards with this group. The fourth term card shows Truman, but Roosevelt was already president, so it stays off boards with this group; dormant until a third posted card fits.

groups.link: All three took place in California.
groups.source: Places in each record: the Mustang first flew at Mines Field, Los Angeles (No. 020); the H-4 flew over Long Beach Harbor (No. 034); Tule Lake is near Newell in northern California (No. 038). The Fu-Go photo was taken at Moffett Field, California, and a balloon was found off its coast, so both stay off boards with this group.

groups.link: In each, Hitler ordered his troops to hold their ground at all costs.
groups.source: Hitler ordered Aachen held at all costs (No. 009). During Supercharge, on 3 November 1942, he ordered Rommel to stand fast and yield not a yard (Nos. 033 and 037, Rommel Papers). His later no retreat order at Stalingrad is famous, so the Stalingrad card stays off boards with this group. Supercharge and the Alamein retreat share the same order, so Supercharge stays off boards with this group; dormant until a third posted card fits.

groups.link: In each, an American general came ashore from the sea.
groups.source: MacArthur waded ashore at Leyte (No. 007); Mark Clark paddled ashore from HMS Seraph near Cherchell (No. 011); Patton went ashore at Fedala from USS Augusta during Torch (No. 045). Marine generals also landed on Bougainville, so it stays off boards with this group.

groups.link: Each involves General George S. Patton.
groups.source: Patton commanded Torch's Western Task Force, landing near Casablanca (No. 045), and his Third Army opened the Lorraine offensive (No. 047). Dormant until a third posted card fits; Koenigsmacker (14 Nov) will.

groups.link: Each involves the U.S. 1st Infantry Division.
groups.source: The 1st Infantry Division helped take Aachen (No. 009) and landed near Oran in Torch's Center Task Force (U.S. Army official history, Northwest Africa). Dormant until a third posted card fits.
